looks_like_me_why: The face has some of my most recognisable features — the silver bob, the glasses frame, the gentle smile and the pearl earrings — so at a glance I can tell it’s meant to be me. However the images are heavily stylised and sometimes the proportions and age feel off. On the cover and a few pages (for example pages 1 and 4) the likeness reads best. On many of the action pages (pages 6–15) the face is exaggerated to fit the cartoony body and large-eyed style, and on a few pages the glasses and facial details are inconsistent, which makes the personalization feel uneven.
rings_true_why: The text follows the familiar Little Red Riding Hood beats and the pictures match the lines closely, so it feels like the real fairy tale and like a child’s picture book. The language is simple and readable for young listeners and the pacing is mostly right. It does feel a bit condensed in places — the wolf’s schemes and the rescue happen very quickly — but for a short personalised book that economy works.
professional_why: The artwork is high quality: consistent 3-D style, lovely color palette, clear compositions and expressive characters. It looks like something a small publisher could print. I docked one point because the face-personalization is inconsistent across pages (glasses, age cues and proportions change) and a couple of scenes feel rushed in the story flow. Those small issues would make me hesitate before gifting without reviewing a final proof.
not_good: Inconsistent facial details and age: the character sometimes looks older and sometimes very childlike (pages 3–7 and 11–15 show the biggest mismatch). The glasses are present on some spreads but missing or altered on others (notably on some of the action pages). The rescue sequence is abrupt — the woodcutter arrives very suddenly (page 15) and the wolf’s exit feels hurried (page 16), which weakens the drama. A couple of frames (page 13 with the wolf baring teeth, page 14–15 chase scenes) might be too intense for very young or sensitive children.
liked: I liked the overall charm and warmth of the illustrations, the bright, friendly color scheme, and the clear visual storytelling. The cottage and forest backgrounds are lovely, and Grandma’s reveal (page 17) and the family table scene (page 18) are particularly cozy and satisfying. The text is simple and rhythmic, perfect for reading aloud to a second grader.
